content.text:
The drawing shows a sulfamide, R-NH-SO2-NH-Ar, with these parts:

- **Imidazole:** N1 is the NH, C2 carries a phenyl, C4 carries the CH2CH2 chain, and C5 carries a 4-methoxyphenyl. In the drawing, the upper N (no H) sits next to the carbon bearing the chain, and the lower NH sits next to the carbon bearing the methoxyphenyl.
- **Chain:** two CH2 groups link the imidazole to the sulfamide NH.
- **Aryl ring:** the NH is attached to a ring carbon. Its ortho position carries the pyrrolidin-1-yl group. The CF3 sits on the carbon that is meta to the NH-bearing carbon, going via the CH between them. Numbering from the NH carbon as C1, the pyrrolidine is at C2 and the CF3 at C5.

Imidazole SMILES: c1(CCNS(=O)(=O)N...)nc(-c2ccccc2)[nH]c1-c1ccc(OC)cc1

Aryl ring: c1(N...)cc(C(F)(F)F)ccc1N1CCCC1. The NH carbon is bonded to the CH, which is bonded to the C-CF3 carbon, so CF3 is at C5. The ring continues through two CH carbons to the carbon bearing the pyrrolidine at C2, which closes back to C1.

SMILES: O=S(=O)(NCCc1nc(-c2ccccc2)[nH]c1-c1ccc(OC)cc1)Nc1cc(C(F)(F)F)ccc1N1CCCC1
